Hi all — quick summary from product/security side after a brief runbook review: we can support tenant-scoped retention exceptions for session/debug traces but there are constraints and evidence we should prepare. Questions and notes below.

What we need from Helix to scope the exception:
- Exact list of namespaces/tenant IDs to be retained (not whole account).
- Which log classes they require: application debug traces, agent-side session logs, server audit logs, or full request-response bodies. Each has different storage and compliance implications.
- Whether the data includes PHI/PII (affects redaction/keystore handling).

What Redwood can provide and artifacts for SIG/CAIQ:
- Retention override mechanics: policy tag on tenant objects + TTL engine exemption; automated label and expiry records captured in the policy audit log (we can export change events).
- Proof-of-delete: we can provide an export that includes the deletion job id, timestamps, object identifiers, and a signed hash (SHA256) of the deletion manifest. We also keep an immutable job log for deletion operations for 1 year.
- Keystore rotation: we can deliver the KMS rotation schedule and key versions used for the tenant; note that for private deployments Helix can use their own KMS.
- Access logs: per-request access logs (index entries) for the retention-exempt objects can be exported as CSV for the requested window.

Limitations / compliance notes:
- We do not retain raw request bodies for >30d by default. Extending to 120d for bodies increases exposure; recommend Helix limit exception to debug traces and audit indices only.
- For PII in traces we require either Helix to accept redaction or to use their own private deployment/KMS for full-body retention.

I'll prepare a small artifact pack today: redwood_deletion_runbook_v2.pdf (internal runbook excerpt) and a sample proof-of-delete manifest. Sophie, can you confirm the tenant IDs and whether Helix will accept redaction for sensitive fields?

Attachments (from Redwood): redwood_deletion_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf), sample_delete_manifest.json (json)
